title: Check if Array is Palindrome
statement:
Write a function that checks if an array of integers `nums` is a palindrome.

An array is a palindrome if it reads the exact same forwards and backwards. Return `true` if it is a palindrome, and `false` otherwise.

examples.explanation: The array is symmetric: first and last elements match, etc.
Forwards is [1,2,3,4,5], backwards is [5,4,3,2,1], which are not identical.

editorial.approach: Use a two-pointer approach, comparing nums[left] and nums[right]. Increment left and decrement right. If any mismatch occurs, return false. Otherwise, return true.

hints: A palindrome array is symmetric. The element at index `i` must equal the element at index `length - 1 - i`.
Check if `nums[left] === nums[right]` on each iteration. Move them closer to the center, and return false if they mismatch.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Create a reversed copy of the array and compare it element-by-element with the original array.

optimizedSolution.explanation: Check symmetry in-place from both ends using two pointers, avoiding extra array allocations.

interviewExplanation: Instead of allocating space to copy and reverse the array (O(n) space), we use a two-pointer strategy. We scan from outside in, comparing opposite ends. This runs in O(n) time and O(1) space.
